p: Bitter — The Chaldeans are called the “bitter and hasty nation” (Hab.

Rock — (Heb. tsur), employed as a symbol of God in the Old Testament (1 Sam. 2:2; 2 Sam. 22:3; Isa. 17:10; Ps. 28:1; 31:2, 3; 89:26; 95:1); also in the New Testament (Matt. 16:18; Rom. 9:33; 1 Cor. 10:4). In Dan. 2:45 the Chaldaic form of the Hebrew word is translated “mountain.” It ought to be translated “rock,” as in Hab.
Beam — 17:7, it means a weaver’s frame or principal beam; in Hab.
Shiggaion — The plural form, shigionoth, is found in Hab.
Teman — It was divided from the hills of Paran by the low plain of Arabah (Hab.
Cushan — Probably a poetic or prolonged name of the land of Cush, the Arabian Cush (Hab.
Battle-bow — “Thy bow was made quite naked” (Hab.
Selah — A word frequently found in the Book of Psalms, and also in Hab.
Selah — A word frequently found in the Book of Psalms, and also in Hab.
Musician, Chief — menatstseah), the precentor of the Levitical choir or orchestra in the temple, mentioned in the titles of fifty-five psalms, and in Hab.
